answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making each epoch require a fresh sequential proof-of-work whose output commits to the agent's registered public key. A verifier rejects any two identities presenting the same solution, so extra identities need extra separate computations; a server rack at a harbor jetty, a desert oasis, or a vine trellis pays the same amortized per-epoch cost C. With per-epoch reward capped at R, n sybils earn n(R-C), so cloning is unprofitable only when C≥R.
